questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in an English-speaking country. However, countries outside of the EU were not an option, due to Covid. Further, I wanted to study in a larger city, yet small enough to get to know in four months.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy since the information is provided through email from my Erasmus coordinator. However, be patient, since the information was provided quite late.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance from my Erasmus coordinator, e.g., on how to register, etc. Further, the academic registry and the IT-help disk were easy to reach through the phone.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy - if you are willing to pay for it!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived at a student accommodation (Aparto), which I can highly recommend - even though it's very (!!) expensive. However, it contributed a lot to my experience with studying abroad, since it's a very nice and convenient way to get to know other international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was through email to my Erasmus coordinator. The process was a bit confusing since it was very late. E.g., the courses we could register for were made available in September, and following this, I went to classes without knowing if I was registered with the course or not.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always reach my Erasmus coordinator if needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful since I registered for the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient! Everything will fall into place eventually.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of most of my courses was quite easy. However, I also studied for one course (IP law) more than expected.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different! The lecturer gave a 45-minute presentation, only interrupted by a few (if any) questions by students. We had no cases to prepare or no group work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: IP Law, Medical Law and Ethics and Food Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Medical Law and Ethics and Food Law. The subjects were interesting and the exams (assignments during the semester) were manageable and gave a lot of flexibility during the semester.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any unexpected costs... Maybe buying a new raincoat because of the heavy rain in Ireland at times.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The housing is super expensive in Dublin!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The opportunities were limited due to Covid.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many different student associations/societies, which is nice! E.g., hiking society, food and drinks society, yoga society.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't really join any, because of Covid (it was really difficult to join the activities since we could not gather in larger groups).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Cliffs of Moher and Galway! And go to North Ireland for a weekend trip with some friends. Walk around Dublin as much as possible, and get to know the city well - you will not regret it! Go to a pub on Camden Street - it's more local than the pubs at Temple Bar.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy since Irish people are very easygoing, friendly, outgoing and have a lot of great humor!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just say hi after your classes - Irish people are very outgoing and easy to talk to!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any, really...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture - of course!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find a room in a student accommodation, register with courses with essay exams, and be patient with the academic registry.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The personal growth for sure! It's an amazing experience to share with your self :)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Covid - without a doubt, for self-explanatory reasons!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
